about.title: Texas roots. Hands-on thinking. Serious capability.
text: Integrated Machine & Hydraulics, LLC brings hydraulic repair, machining and system solutions together in Santa Fe, Texas.
Equipment problems rarely stop at a single component. That is why IMH brings repair, machining, manufacturing and hydraulic system capabilities into one conversation.
Our mission is to deliver dependable hydraulic and mechanical solutions, build lasting customer relationships and approach each job with integrity, precision and care.
From a cylinder repair to a custom power unit, our focus is the same: understand what your equipment needs and help you move forward.
about.imageAlt: Container cranes and stacked containers at a port terminal

faqs.q: What should I send with a repair inquiry?
faqs.a: Send the equipment type, manufacturer and model if known, a description of the problem and your contact details. Tag photos, overall photos and close-ups of damage help the team understand the job.

faqs.q: Can you help if I do not know which part has failed?
faqs.a: Yes. Start with the equipment and symptoms. IMH provides diagnostics and troubleshooting; the next step depends on the system and the issue.

faqs.q: Do you offer more than component repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. IMH offers machining, fabrication, custom manufacturing, hydraulic power units, automation and control solutions, plus field service and inspections.

faqs.q: How do I get pricing and turnaround information?
faqs.a: Contact IMH with your equipment details. Pricing, scope and timing depend on the component, condition, required parts and availability. No turnaround is promised by this website.

faqs.q: Where is the shop, and when is it open?
faqs.a: 15921 Pine Street, Santa Fe, Texas 77517. Monday through Friday, 7AM–5PM Central. Closed Saturday and Sunday. Call before arranging a drop-off or site visit.

facts.heading: Industries Served
items: Construction and heavy equipment: excavators, earthmoving equipment and the hydraulic components that carry the load, with cylinder, pump, motor and machining support.
Marine: hydraulic pumps and cylinders through to marine gearboxes and winches.
Ports and stevedoring: hydraulic repair, component replacement and custom manufacturing for cargo handling equipment.
Industrial manufacturing: hydraulic power units, control systems, precision components and field service.
Oil and gas: hydraulic repair, power units and custom machine parts for energy applications.
Utility vehicles: fleet hydraulics, cylinders, pumps and system upgrades.

facts.heading: How A Repair Starts
items: Tell us what failed: the symptoms, equipment details and timing, with photos of the component and tag.
Define the repair: inspection, repair or replacement options, because the right scope comes before the work.
Put expertise to work: hydraulic repair, machining and system capabilities together for the needs of the job.
Plan the return: coordinate the next steps with the team so the equipment can get back to your operation.

facts.heading: Capability Sheets
facts.text: IMH publishes capability overviews for construction and heavy equipment, marine, ports and stevedoring, industrial manufacturing, oil and gas, and utility vehicles. Contact the shop to discuss current scope and availability.

facts.heading: What To Send With An Inquiry
items: Manufacturer, model and serial number
What the equipment is doing
Photos of the tag and damaged areas
Your location and required timing

facts.heading: Useful Details By Service
items: Cylinders: equipment type and cylinder application, photos of the cylinder, tag and visible damage, and what changed - leaks, drift, loss of force or damaged components.
Pumps and motors: manufacturer, model and serial number, the equipment application and operating symptoms, and photos of the nameplate and connections.
Valves: valve manufacturer and complete part number, photos of the tag, ports and electrical connectors, and a description of the motion or pressure issue.
Machining: drawings or dimensions when available, part material and application, and photos of the existing part and damaged areas.
Power units: the application and equipment the unit serves, existing pressure, flow and electrical details if known, and photos, drawings or the target outcome.
Automation and controls: photos of the existing panel and equipment, electrical diagrams or PLC details if available, and the fault symptoms and the operation you need to achieve.
Marine: the vessel or equipment application, gearbox, winch or component tag information, and the failure symptoms and required timing.
Field service: the site address and access requirements, equipment type and failure symptoms, and photos with your scheduling requirements.
